links.outcome: ChatGPT-4 radiotherapy recommendations versus tumor board, independent specialist, and guidelines on same cases
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 agreed with tumor board in 76% (κ=0.61) and with independent specialist in 79%; specialist overall agreement was 90%; AI showed overtreatment bias (p<0.05).
links.quote: Its overall agreement (76%) was lower than that of the human specialist (90%).

links.outcome: AI handling of borderline/complex decisions without deferring, over-recommending treatment
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 omitted some indicated treatments in straightforward cases (sensitivity ~73%) and suggested unnecessary therapy in borderline cases (intermediate specificity 64.7%); overtreatment bias p<0.05.
links.quote: However, it cannot substitute for human judgment: the AI omitted some indicated treatments in straightforward cases and suggested unnecessary therapy in some borderline cases, indicating a lack of nuanced clinical reasoning.

screen.reason: The study evaluated ChatGPT-4's performance on prospective clinical cases compared to a multidisciplinary tumor board and guidelines, measuring model accuracy/agreement rather than testing a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
